concerns.text: T005's full grid sweeps '{None, BiasCorrected, VarianceInflated} adjustments', i.e. it consumes the adjustment code, but the canonical execution order lists T005 BEFORE T006 which implements `code/analysis/adjustments.py` and wires it into `ci_builder.py`. The trailing caveat ('T006's implementation may land before T005's execution') acknowledges the inversion but leaves the stated order consumer-before-producer. Swap the order to T006 → T005 (or split T005 into implementation and execution) so the dependency is structural, not a footnote.

T009 is tagged [P] (parallel-safe) but its description says 'if flagged, increase N_SIM for those conditions and re-run them' — re-running conditions implies rewriting rows in `data/results/coverage_results.csv`, shared mutable state produced by T005 and consumed by T007/T008/T010. A task that can mutate the SSoT results file is not parallel-safe. Either remove the [P] tag or specify that re-runs write to a separate file merged by a later sequential task.

T010 re-runs 'the documented workflow end-to-end', regenerating `coverage_results.csv` and downstream artifacts, while T11 (also [P]) reads those same artifacts to write `research_results.md`. Two [P] tasks where one rewrites the files the other reads is an unsafe parallel pair with an implicit ordering requirement (T010 must complete before T11's numbers are final). Remove [P] from at least one and state the sequence.

T004's pilot writes rows into `data/results/coverage_results.csv` and T005 writes 'all rows' to the same file. The overwrite/append relationship is unstated; state explicitly that the full run replaces the pilot rows (or the pilot writes a separate pilot file) so T007/T008 don't ingest pilot rows with N_SIM=50.
